calibration.description: deterministic formal evaluation; no confidence or probability output exists

candidate.description: rdam.dung (rdam 6.0.0): exhaustive-subset evaluation of grounded, complete, preferred, and stable semantics, capacity 14 arguments; input origin recorded as supplied or explicitly derived from a named upstream result

compatibility.environment: pixi production environment (editable install of the single rdam distribution) and default environment; tests/dung and production-boundary inspection
compatibility.evidence: pure Python, no I/O at import; the rdam distribution declares every runtime dependency in pyproject [project.dependencies]; production-boundary valid with rdam.dung inside the one production package

decided_by: Claude Fable 5.1 — authored from the committed tests and measurements under the owner rulings of 2026-09-02 ('build it all'; one rdam package, one wheel); licence ruling: own code under the repository MIT licence

latency.platform: Apple Silicon (Apple M5 Max), CPython 3.14, pixi default environment

licensing.decision_note: own code under the repository's MIT licence; no third-party model or corpus is involved
licensing.intended_use: local, single-person discourse analysis on this machine
licensing.licence: MIT (repository LICENSE; own code, no trained assets)

correctness_arguments: conflict-freeness, acceptability, admissibility, completeness, grounded (least fixed point of the characteristic function, monotone so iteration terminates), preferred (maximal complete), stable (complete attacking every outsider) implemented as stated in Dung 1995; see rdam/dung/semantics.py docstring

complete extensions are found by exhaustive enumeration of all 2^|Ar| candidate sets under a declared capacity, so the result is exact by construction; inputs beyond capacity are refused, never approximated
grounded is computed independently by fixed-point iteration and checked against the enumerated complete extensions (least element, intersection of all complete)

the provider never derives a framework: input_origin is 'supplied', or 'explicitly_derived' with the caller's named upstream result identity copied verbatim (FR-016); the semantics evaluated are identical in both cases
property_tests: tests/dung/test_semantics.py::TestKnownFrameworks (single argument, simple attack, mutual attack, odd cycle without stable extension, self-attack, reinstatement chain)
tests/dung/test_semantics.py::TestInvariants::test_random_frameworks_up_to_capacity_satisfy_the_definitions (200 seeded random frameworks, up to eight arguments)

tests/dung/test_provider.py (through the machine: supplied framework in, typed failures, capacity refusal, unavailable without a decision naming this source, explicitly derived input names its upstream result)
tests/machine/test_machine.py::TestLineage (a declared derivation becomes lineage naming the exact upstream artifact and both provider identities)

limitations: exhaustive enumeration: capacity is 14 arguments; larger frameworks need a labelling-based algorithm in a new candidate
semantics limited to grounded, complete, preferred, stable; semi-stable, ideal, and stage semantics are not provided
evaluates supplied or caller-derived frameworks only; no extraction from text (by design, FR-016)
strengths: exact by construction under the declared capacity
invariants verified exhaustively for three-argument frameworks and on seeded random frameworks
typed refusal of malformed or over-capacity input
supplied versus explicitly derived input is recorded, never inferred
recommendation.summary: Replace the previous rdam.dung source with the same semantics plus explicit input-origin recording: exact formal semantics with correctness arguments and property tests, deterministic, measured latency, no licensing constraint.
